Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *stenàti.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈstɛnɐ]
  • Rhymes: -ɛnɐ
  • Syllabification(key): сте‧на
This entry needs an audio pronunciation. If you are a native speaker with a microphone, please record this word. The recorded pronunciation will appear here when it's ready.

Verb

[edit]

сте́на • (sténa) first-singular present indicative, impf

  1. (intransitive) to groan, to moan
    сте́на от болка ― sténa ot bolka ― to groan out of pain

Etymology 2

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *stěna, reflecting an earlier *staiˀnāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *steyh₂- (“to stiffen”).

Noun

[edit]

стена́ • (stená) f (dialectal, obsolete)

  1. rock, crag
    Synonyms: скала́ (skalá), канара́ (kanará)

Etymology 3

[edit]

Either a secondary meaning of Etymology 2 or from a different *stěna, reflecting an earlier *stēˀgsnāˀ, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)teg- (“to cover”). Many scholars do not draw etymological distinction between the two senses.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [stɛˈna]
  • Rhymes: -na
  • Syllabification(key): сте‧на
This entry needs an audio pronunciation. If you are a native speaker with a microphone, please record this word. The recorded pronunciation will appear here when it's ready.

Noun

[edit]

стена́ • (stená) f (relational adjective сте́нен) (standard)

  1. wall (of a building)
    стена на стая ― stena na staja ― a room's wall
    язовирна стена ― jazovirna stena ― a dam's wall
  2. (geometry) wall; face (any of the flat bounding surfaces of a polyhedron)
    фигура с четири стени ― figura s četiri steni ― a figure with four faces
  3. (figurative) wall (that which isolates and separates people socially)
Usage
[edit]

стена (stena) refers to any sort of external surface, regardless of make-up. Hyponyms зид (zid), дувар (duvar) specifically denote built-up walls, made of stone or bricks.

Russian

[edit]

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *stěna, see also English stone and stain.

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • стѣна́ (stěná) — pre-1918 spelling

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [sʲtʲɪˈna]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

стена́ • (stená) f inan (genitive стены́, nominative plural сте́ны, genitive plural стен, relational adjective стенно́й, diminutive сте́нка or сте́ночка)

  1. wall
    запере́ться в четырёх стена́х ― zaperétʹsja v četyrjóx stenáx ― to immure oneself (literally, “to lock up oneself up in four walls”)
    би́ться голово́й об сте́ну ― bítʹsja golovój ob sténu ― to beat one's head against the wall
    как об сте́ну горо́х ― kak ob sténu goróx ― like talking to a wall
    как за ка́менной стено́й ― kak za kámennoj stenój ― safe (literally, “like behind a stone wall”)
    • 1905, Фёдор Сологуб [Fyodor Sologub], chapter XX, in Мелкий бес; English translation from John Cournos and Richard Aldington, transl., The Little Demon, New York: Alfred A. Knopf, 1916:
      "Что ж, ка́жется, всё хорошо́: запрещённых кни́жек не ви́дно, лампа́дки те́плятся, ца́рские портре́ты вися́т на стене́, на почётном ме́сте".
      "Što ž, kážetsja, vsjo xorošó: zapreščónnyx knížek ne vídno, lampádki tépljatsja, cárskije portréty visját na stené, na počótnom méste".
      " Well, everything seems all right—there are no forbidden books visible, the ikon-lamps are alight, the Royal portraits are hanging in the place of honour on the wall."
